subject: dm
title: Seven-bit union
prompt: How many bit strings of length 7 start with 00 or end with 111?

solution.text: Starting with 00 leaves 5 free bits: 2^5=32.
Ending with 111 leaves 4 free bits: 2^4=16. Both conditions leave 2 free bits: 2^2=4.
By inclusion-exclusion: 32+16-4=44.

conceptNote: Identify distinct outcomes and overlaps first. For a minimum guarantee, show both the forcing threshold and why one fewer can avoid the event.

subject: dm
title: Eight-bit intersection
prompt: How many 8-bit strings start with 10 and end with 01?

solution.text: The prescribed first two and last two positions do not overlap.
Four positions are free, each with 2 choices.
There are 2^4=16 strings.

title: Birthday months
prompt: How many people guarantee two with the same birth month?

solution.text: There are 12 month boxes.
With 12 people, one person per month is still possible.
The 13th person forces a repeated month. Answer: 13.

subject: dm
title: Three matching residues
prompt: How many integers guarantee three in the same residue class modulo 5?

solution.text: There are 5 residue boxes.
At most 2 in each box permits 10 integers without a triple.
The next integer forces a triple: 5*(3-1)+1=11.

subject: dm
title: Professors and scores
prompt: Six professors give integer scores from 0 through 60. How many students guarantee two with the same professor and score?

solution.text: Use a box for each ordered pair (professor,score).
There are 6*61=366 boxes, since both 0 and 60 are included.
With 367 students, two share a box. With 366, one per box is possible. Thus the minimum is 367.

title: Product rule with no repetition
prompt: How many 3-letter codes can be made from A,B,C,D,E without repeating letters?

solution.text: There are 5 choices for the first letter, 4 for the second and 3 for the third.
By the product rule, 5*4*3=60.
Order matters because the objects are codes.

subject: dm
title: Identical programs pigeonhole
prompt: An alphabet has 128 characters. Students submit nonempty strings of length at most 100. What minimum class size guarantees two identical submissions?

solution.text: There are 128^i strings of length i. All nonempty lengths 1 through 100 are possible boxes.
The number of boxes is S=sum_(i=1)^100 128^i=(128^101-128)/127.
S submissions could all be distinct. By the pigeonhole principle S+1 submissions force a duplicate.
Minimum = (128^101-128)/127+1. This exact expression is preferable to expanding the very large integer.

conceptNote: Identify distinct outcomes and overlaps first. For a minimum guarantee, show both the forcing threshold and why one fewer can avoid the event.
